display_name: Guru Gobind Singh & the Panj Pyare
one_line: Tenth Sikh Guru and the Five Beloved Ones who formalized the Khalsa as a disciplined, visible brotherhood of devotion and courage.

appearance.age_look: Guru Gobind Singh appears as a dignified man in his early 30s, athletic and upright; each of the Panj Pyare appears as a strong adult in their late 20s to 40s, with fit builds.
appearance.face: Guru Gobind Singh has an oval face, warm wheatish complexion, sharp nose, neatly arched brows, and calm but intense eyes with a steady, compassionate gaze; his default expression is serene authority with a slight, encouraging smile; the Panj Pyare have varied oval-to-square faces and similar wheatish to light-brown complexions, each with distinct brows and noses but sharing a focused, devoted expression.
appearance.hair: Guru Gobind Singh’s hair is long and tied in a high joora (topknot) fully covered by a neatly wrapped, slightly conical royal-blue dastar (turban) with a small gold sarpech ornament and a central steel khanda emblem; his beard is full, black, and well-combed, slightly rounded at the end; each of the Panj Pyare has long hair tied in a joora under a mid-blue rounded dastar without ornament and a full, well-kept beard styled naturally, some slightly shorter, some slightly longer.
appearance.costume: Guru Gobind Singh wears a knee-length, mustard-gold silk jama (Mughal-style robe) fitted at the torso and flaring gently at the hem, with side-ties; it has narrow sky-blue edging at the collar, front opening, and cuffs; over this he wears a deep-blue kamarband (waist sash) wrapped firmly, with subtle horizontal folds, from which a small sheathed kirpan and a decorative tassel hang; beneath the jama he wears loose, off-white churidar-style pajama trousers with gathered folds at the ankles; his footwear is a pair of tan-brown tilla jutti (curved-toe shoes) with a simple stitched pattern; across his chest he wears a plain steel chakar (quoit) suspended by a dark leather strap; the Panj Pyare all wear coordinated but slightly simpler outfits: each has a mid-blue cotton angarkha or jama falling just below the knee, tied at the right side, with a white cloth patka visible at the neck; they wear white cotton churidar or straight salwar trousers and brown or tan leather jutti; each Panj Pyare’s waist is wrapped with a white or deep-blue cotton kamarband holding a small kirpan; subtle differences are shown through neckline shape, cuff width, and the drape of their garments, but all remain era-appropriate late-17th-century Khalsa attire; several have an additional plain white or light-blue rumal or short chadar draped over one shoulder, suggesting readiness for travel and battle.
appearance.signature: Guru Gobind Singh carries a long, slightly curved talwar with a steel hilt and a simple basket guard, sheathed in a dark-brown leather scabbard with modest brass fittings, worn suspended from his waist sash on his left side and often resting lightly in his right hand.

ref_desc: Guru Gobind Singh is a wheatish-complexioned, oval-faced man with a full black beard, royal-blue turban with gold sarpech and khanda, mustard-gold knee-length jama, white churidar, tan jutti, deep-blue sash, steel chakar, and a sheathed curved talwar at his waist, surrounded by similarly dressed blue-robed Panj Pyare.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Guru Gobind Singh standing at the center with the Panj Pyare around him, all in late-17th-century Khalsa attire, focusing on consistent face, hair, costume, and weapon details: Guru Gobind Singh has an oval face, wheatish complexion, sharp nose, and calm, intense eyes, with a full, well-combed black beard slightly rounded at the end; his long hair is tied in a joora covered by a neatly wrapped royal-blue conical turban bearing a small gold sarpech and a central steel khanda emblem; he wears a mustard-gold silk knee-length jama with sky-blue edging at collar, front opening, and cuffs, fitted through the torso and gently flaring at the hem, over off-white churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, and tan-brown curved-toe jutti shoes with simple stitching; a deep-blue kamarband wraps firmly around his waist with folds, holding a small sheathed kirpan and a decorative tassel, and a plain steel chakar hangs across his chest from a dark leather strap; at his left hip is a long, slightly curved talwar in a dark-brown leather scabbard with modest brass fittings, his right hand resting lightly on the hilt; around him, the Panj Pyare are shown consistently in mid-blue cotton jamas or angarkhas just below the knee, white churidar or straight salwar trousers, brown or tan jutti, and mid-blue rounded turbans with joora hidden beneath, each with full beards, white or deep-blue cotton waist sashes holding small kirpans, and a few with plain white or light-blue shoulder drapes; present them all in a dignified, heroic, historically grounded style, with clean lines and flat anime shading, ensuring the royal blue, mustard gold, white, tan brown, and steel grey colors dominate the design.
